{{Hatnote|This article is about the numbers 700 through 799; for each individual number, see its section below.}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=March 2025}}
{{Infobox number
| number = 700
|lang1=[[Armenian numerals|Armenian]]|lang1 symbol=Չ|lang2=[[Hebrew numerals|Hebrew]]|lang2 symbol=<span style="font-size:150%;">ת"ש / ן</span>|lang3=[[Babylonian cuneiform numerals|Babylonian cuneiform]]|lang3 symbol=𒌋𒐕𒐏|lang4=[[Egyptian numerals|Egyptian hieroglyph]]|lang4 symbol=<span style="font-size:200%;">𓍨</span>}}
'''700''' ('''seven hundred''') is the [[natural number]] following 699 and preceding 701.

It is a [[composite number]] and the sum of four consecutive [[Prime number|prime]]s (167 + 173 + 179 + 181).

==Integers from 701 to 799==
===700s===

==== 701 ====
701 is a prime number, a [[Chen prime]], an [[Eisenstein prime]] with no imaginary part, and the sum of three consecutive primes (229 + 233 + 239).
==== 702 ====
702 = 2 × 3<sup>3</sup> × 13. It is a [[pronic number]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A002378|title=Sloane's A002378 : Oblong (or promic, pronic, or heteromecic) numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> a [[nontotient]], and a Harshad number.
==== 703 ====
703 = 19 × 37. It is a [[hexagonal number]],<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A000384|title=Sloane's A000384 : Hexagonal numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> a [[Kaprekar number]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A006886|title=Sloane's A006886 : Kaprekar numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> and the 37th [[triangular number]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A000217|title=Sloane's A000217 : Triangular numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> It is the smallest number requiring 73 fifth powers for Waring representation.

703 is commonly found in the formula for [[body mass index]].

==== 704 ====
704 = 2<sup>6</sup> × 11. It is a [[Harshad number]] and a [[Lazy caterer's sequence|lazy caterer number]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=A000124 - OEIS |url=https://oeis.org/A000124 |access-date=2026-07-04 |website=oeis.org}}</ref>

==== 705 ====
705 = 3 × 5 × 47. It is a [[sphenic number]] the smallest [[Lucas pseudoprime|Bruckman-Lucas pseudoprime]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=A005845 - OEIS |url=https://oeis.org/A005845 |access-date=2026-07-04 |website=oeis.org}}</ref>
==== 706 ====
706 = 2 × 353. It is a nontotient a [[Smith number]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A006753|title=Sloane's A006753 : Smith numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>
==== 707 ====
707 = 7 × 101. It is a [[palindromic number]] and the sum of five consecutive primes (131 + 137 + 139 + 149 + 151). There are 707 lattice paths from (0,0) to (5,5) with steps (0,1), (1,0) and, when on the diagonal, (1,1).<ref>{{cite OEIS|A026671|Number of lattice paths from (0,0) to (n,n) with steps (0,1), (1,0) and, when on the diagonal, (1,1)|access-date=2022-05-22}}</ref>

==== 708 ====
708 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 3 × 59. There are 708 partitions of 28 that do not contain 1 as a part.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A002865|Number of partitions of n that do not contain 1 as a part|access-date=2022-06-02}}</ref>

==== 709 ====
709 is a prime number and a [[happy number]].

It is the seventh in the series 2, 3, 5, 11, 31, 127, 709 where each number is the nth prime with n being the number preceding it in the series, therefore, it is a prime index number.

===710s===

==== 710 ====
710 = 2 × 5 × 71. It is a sphenic number and a nontotient. There are 710 forests with 11 vertices.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hougardy |first1=Stefan |title=Classes of perfect graphs |journal=Discrete Mathematics |date=October 2006 |volume=306 |issue=19–20 |pages=2529–2571 |doi=10.1016/j.disc.2006.05.021 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite OEIS|A005195|Number of forests with n unlabeled nodes|access-date=2022-05-22}}</ref>
==== 711 ====
{{Redirect|711 (number)|the phone number|Telecommunications relay service|5=711 (disambiguation)}}
711 = 3<sup>2</sup> × 79. It is a Harshad number. There are 711 planar Berge perfect graphs on 7 nodes.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A123449|Number of planar Berge perfect graphs on n nodes}}</ref>

==== 712 ====
712 = 2<sup>3</sup> × 89. It is a [[refactorable number]], the totient sum for first 48 integers, and the sum of the first twenty-one primes.

It is the largest known number such that it and its 8th power (66,045,000,696,445,844,586,496) have no common digits.

==== 713 ====
713 = 23 × 31. It is a [[Blum integer]]. 

In [[Judaism]] there are 713 letters on a [[Mezuzah]] scroll.

==== 714 ====
714 = 2 × 3 × 7 × 17. It is a nontotient and a balanced number, and the sum of twelve consecutive primes (37 + 41 + 43 + 47 + 53 + 59 + 61 + 67 + 71 + 73 + 79 + 83).<ref>{{cite OEIS|A020492|Balanced numbers: numbers k such that phi(k) (A000010) divides sigma(k) (A000203)}}</ref> It forms a [[Ruth–Aaron pair]] with 715 (either definition). It is the sum of twelve consecutive primes (37 + 41 + 43 + 47 + 53 + 59 + 61 + 67 + 71 + 73 + 79 + 83).

The product of 714 and 715 is the product of the first 7 prime numbers (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, and 17).

==== 715 ====
715 = 5 × 11 × 13. It is a sphenic number, a pentagonal number,<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A000326|title=Sloane's A000326 : Pentagonal numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> and a Harshad number. It forms a Ruth-Aaron pair with 714 (either definition).

It is a [[pentatope number]] because 713=<math>\tbinom {13}4</math>.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A000332|title=Sloane's A000332 : Binomial coefficient binomial(n,4)|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>

The product of 714 and 715 is the product of the first 7 prime numbers (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, and 17).

==== 716 ====
716 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 179.

==== 717 ====
717 = 3 × 239. It is a [[palindromic number]].

==== 718 ====
718 = 2 × 359.

==== 719 ====
719 is a prime number, a [[Sophie Germain prime]],<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A005384|title=Sloane's A005384 : Sophie Germain primes|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> a [[safe prime]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A005385|title=Sloane's A005385 : Safe primes|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> a Chen prime, and an Eisenstein prime with no imaginary part. 

Because 719 = 6! − 1, 719 is a [[factorial prime]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A088054|title=Sloane's A088054 : Factorial primes|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> 

It is the sum of seven consecutive primes (89 + 97 + 101 + 103 + 107 + 109 + 113).

===720s===

==== 720 ====
{{Main|720 (number)}}

==== 721 ====
721 = 7 × 103. It is a [[centered hexagonal number]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A003215|title=Sloane's A003215 : Hex (or centered hexagonal) numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> and the sum of nine consecutive primes (61 + 67 + 71 + 73 + 79 + 83 + 89 + 97 + 101). It is the smallest number that is the difference of two positive cubes in two ways.

==== 722 ====
722 = 2 × 19<sup>2</sup>. It is a nontotient. There are 722 odd parts in all partitions of 15.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A066897|Total number of odd parts in all partitions of n|access-date=2022-05-22}}</ref>

==== 723 ====
723 = 3 × 241. It is the side length of an [[Heronian triangle#Almost-equilateral Heronian triangles|almost-equilateral Heronian triangle]].<ref>{{cite OEIS|A016064|Smallest side lengths of almost-equilateral Heronian triangles|access-date=2022-05-22}}</ref>

==== 724 ====
724 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 181. It is a nontotient and the side length of an [[Heronian triangle#Almost-equilateral Heronian triangles|almost-equilateral Heronian triangle]].<ref>{{cite OEIS|A003500|2=a(n) = 4*a(n-1) - a(n-2) with a(0) = 2, a(1) = 4|access-date=2022-05-22}}</ref> It is the sum of four consecutive primes (173 + 179 + 181 + 191) and the sum of six consecutive primes (107 + 109 + 113 + 127 + 131 + 137). There are 724 [[Eight queens puzzle|''n''-queens problem]] solutions for&nbsp;''n''&nbsp;=&nbsp;10.

==== 725 ====
725 = 5<sup>2</sup> × 29. It is the side length of an [[Heronian triangle#Almost-equilateral Heronian triangles|almost-equilateral Heronian triangle]].<ref>{{cite OEIS|A335025|Largest side lengths of almost-equilateral Heronian triangles|access-date=2022-05-22}}</ref>

==== 726 ====
726 = 2 × 3 × 11<sup>2</sup>. It is a [[pentagonal pyramidal number]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A002411|title=Sloane's A002411 : Pentagonal pyramidal numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>

==== 727 ====
727 is a prime number, a [[palindromic prime]], and a [[lucky prime]].<ref name=":6">{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A031157|title=Sloane's A031157 : Numbers that are both lucky and prime|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>
==== 728 ====
728 = 2<sup>3</sup> × 7 × 13. It is a nontotient, a [[Smith number]],<ref name=":3" /> and a [[cabtaxi number]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A047696|title=Sloane's A047696 : Smallest positive number that can be written in n ways as a sum of two (not necessarily positive) cubes|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> There are 728 [[oeis:A005897|cubes of edge length 1 required to make a hollow cube of edge length 12]].There are 728 [[oeis:A001187|connected graphs on 5 labelled vertices]].

728!! - 1 is prime.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A007749|Numbers k such that k!! - 1 is prime|access-date=2022-05-24}}</ref>

[[oeis:A006316|728<sup>64</sup> + 1 is prime]].

==== 729 ====
729 = 27<sup>2</sup> = 9<sup>3</sup> = 3<sup>6</sup>. It is a [[perfect totient number]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A082897|title=Sloane's A082897 : Perfect totient numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> a Smith number,<ref name=":3" /> and a [[centered octagonal number]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A016754|title=Sloane's A016754 : Odd squares: a(n) = (2n+1)^2. Also centered octagonal numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> It is the largest three-digit cube (9<sup>3</sup>) and the only three-digit sixth power (3<sup>6</sup>).

A [[philosopher king]]'s pleasure is 729 times a tyrant's pleasure according to Plato in the ''[[Republic (Plato)|Republic]].''

===730s===

==== 730 ====
730 = 2 × 5 × 73. It is a sphenic number, a nontotient, and a Harshad number. There are 730 generalized weak orders on 5 points.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A004123|Number of generalized weak orders on n points|access-date=2022-05-22}}</ref>
==== 731 ====
731 = 17 × 43. It is the sum of three consecutive primes (239 + 241 + 251). There are 731 Euler trees with total weight 7.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A007317|Binomial transform of Catalan numbers}}</ref>
==== 732 ====
732 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 3 × 61. It is a Harshad number.

It is the sum of eight consecutive primes (73 + 79 + 83 + 89 + 97 + 101 + 103 + 107) and the sum of ten consecutive primes (53 + 59 + 61 + 67 + 71 + 73 + 79 + 83 + 89 + 97).

There are 732 collections of subsets of {1, 2, 3, 4} that are closed under union and intersection.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A306445|Number of collections of subsets of {1, 2, ..., n} that are closed under union and intersection|access-date=2022-05-22}}</ref>

==== 733 ====
733 is a prime number, a [[balanced prime]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A006562|title=Sloane's A006562 : Balanced primes|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> a [[permutable prime]], and an [[emirp]]. It is the sum of five consecutive primes (137 + 139 + 149 + 151 + 157)
==== 734 ====
734 = 2 × 367. It is a nontotient. There are 734 [[hamiltonian path#Definitions|traceable graphs]] on 7 nodes.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A057864|Number of simple traceable graphs on n nodes|access-date=2022-05-22}}</ref>
==== 735 ====
735 = 3 × 5 × 7<sup>2</sup>. It is a [[Harshad number]] and a Zuckerman number.
* the smallest number such that uses the same digits as its distinct prime factors

==== 736 ====
736 = 2<sup>5</sup> × 23. It is a [[centered heptagonal number]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A069099|title=Sloane's A069099 : Centered heptagonal numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> a [[happy number]], a [[Harshad number]], and a nice [[Friedman number]] since 736 = 7 + 3<sup>6</sup>.
==== 737 ====
737 = 11 × 67. It is a [[palindromic number]] and a [[blum integer]].
==== 738 ====
738 = 2 × 3<sup>2</sup> × 41. It is a Harshad number.

==== 739 ====
739 is a prime number, a lucky prime,<ref name=":6" /> a [[oeis:A006450|prime index prime]], a [[happy number]], and a strictly non-palindromic number.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A016038|title=Sloane's A016038 : Strictly non-palindromic numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>

===740s===

==== 740 ====
740 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 5 × 37. It is a nontotient. There are 740 connected square free graphs on 9 nodes.<ref>{{cite OEIS|
A077269|Number of connected squarefree graphs on n nodes|access-date=2022-05-23}}</ref>
==== 741 ====
741 = 3 × 13 × 19. It is a sphenic number and the 38th [[triangular number]].<ref name=":1" />
==== 742 ====
742 = 2 × 7 × 53. It is a sphenic number, a [[decagonal number]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A001107|title=Sloane's A001107 : 10-gonal (or decagonal) numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> an [[icosahedral number]], and a [[Lazy caterer's sequence|lazy caterer number]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=A000124 - OEIS |url=https://oeis.org/A000124 |access-date=2026-07-05 |website=oeis.org}}</ref> There are 742 partitions of 30 into divisors of 30.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A018818|Number of partitions of n into divisors of n}}</ref>
* the smallest number that is one more than triple its reverse.

==== 743 ====
It is a [[prime number]] and an eisenstein prime with no imaginary part. 743 is a [[Sophie Germain prime]] because 2&#x20;×&#x20;743&#x20;+&#x20;1&#x20;=&#x20;1487 and 1487 is also prime. 743 is an [[emirp]], because 347 (the reversal of its digits) is prime.

There are exactly 743 [[Independent set (graph theory)|independent sets]] in a four-dimensional (16 vertex) [[hypercube graph]], and exactly 743 connected [[Cubic graph|cubic graphs]] with 16 vertices and [[Girth (graph theory)|girth]] four.

==== 744 ====
744 is a [[semiperfect number]]<ref>{{Cite OEIS |A005835 |Pseudoperfect (or semiperfect) numbers n: some subset of the proper divisors of n sums to n. |access-date=2023-04-03}}</ref> and an [[abundant number]].<ref>{{Cite OEIS |A005101 |Abundant numbers (sum of divisors of m exceeds 2m). |access-date=2023-04-03}}</ref><ref name="AbunoN">{{Cite OEIS |A033880 |Abundance of n, or (sum of divisors of n) - 2n. |access-date=2023-12-29}}</ref>

The [[J-invariant|''{{mvar|j}}''-invariant]], an important function in the study of [[Modular form|modular forms]] and [[Monstrous moonshine]], can be written as a [[Fourier series]] in which the constant term is 744:<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Berndt|first1=Bruce C.|author1-link=Bruce C. Berndt|last2=Chan|first2=Heng Huat|year=1999|title=Ramanujan and the modular j-invariant|journal=[[Canadian Mathematical Bulletin]]|volume=42|issue=4|pages=427–440|doi=10.4153/CMB-1999-050-1|mr=1727340|s2cid=1816362|zbl=|doi-access=free}}</ref> <math display="block">j(\tau) = q^{-1} + 744 + 196\,884 q + 21\,493\,760 q^2 + 864\,299\,970 q^3 + \cdots,</math>where <math>q = e^{2\pi i\tau}</math>. One consequence of this is that 744 appears in expressions for [[Ramanujan's constant]] and other [[Almost integer|almost integers]].

==== 745 ====
745 = 5 × 149. There are 745 non-connected simple labeled graphs covering 6 vertices.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A327070|Number of non-connected simple labeled graphs covering n vertices|access-date=2022-05-23}}</ref>

==== 746 ====
746 = 2 × 373. 

It is a nontotient. There are 746 non-normal semi-magic squares with sum of entries equal to 6.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A321719|Number of non-normal semi-magic squares with sum of entries equal to n|access-date=2022-05-30}}</ref>

746=1<sup>5</sup> + 2<sup>4</sup> + 3<sup>6</sup> = 1<sup>7</sup> + 2<sup>4</sup> + 3<sup>6</sup>.

==== 747 ====
747 = 3<sup>2</sup> × 83. It is a [[palindromic number]].

747=<math>\left\lfloor {\frac {4^{23}}{3^{23}}} \right\rfloor</math><ref>{{cite OEIS|A064628|Floor(4^n / 3^n)|access-date=2022-05-30}}</ref>

===== 748 =====
748 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 11 × 17. It is a nontotient, a [[happy number]], and a primitive abundant number.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A091191|title=Sloane's A091191 : Primitive abundant numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>

==== 749 ====
749 = 7 × 107. It is a [[blum integer]] and the sum of three consecutive primes (241 + 251 + 257).
===750s===

==== 750 ====
750 = 2 × 3 × 5<sup>3</sup>. It is an [[nonagonal number|enneagonal number]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A001106|title=Sloane's A001106 : 9-gonal (or enneagonal or nonagonal) numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>

==== 751 ====
751 is a prime number, a Chen prime, and an emirp.

==== 752 ====
752 = 2<sup>4</sup> × 47. It is a nontotient. There are 752 partitions of 11 into parts of 2 kinds<ref>{{cite OEIS|A000712|2=Generating function = Product_{m≥1} 1/(1 - x^m)^2; a(n) = number of partitions of n into parts of 2 kinds|access-date=2022-05-30}}</ref>

==== 753 ====
753 = 3 × 251. It is a [[blum integer]].

==== 754 ====
754 = 2 × 13 × 29. It is a sphenic number, a nontotient, and the totient sum for first 49 integers.

There are 754 different ways to divide a 10 × 10 square into sub-squares.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A034295|Number of different ways to divide an n X n square into sub-squares|access-date=2022-05-23}}</ref>

==== 755 ====
755 = 5 × 151. There are 755 vertices in a regular drawing of the [[oeis:A331755/a331755_10.png|complete bipartite graph K<sub>9,9</sub>]].<ref>{{cite OEIS|A331755|Number of vertices in a regular drawing of the complete bipartite graph K_{n,n}|access-date=2022-05-23}}</ref>

==== 756 ====
756 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 3<sup>3</sup> × 7. It is a pronic number,<ref name=":0" /> a Harshad number, and the sum of six consecutive primes (109 + 113 + 127 + 131 + 137 + 139).
==== 757 ====
757 is a prime number, a palindromic prime, a [[happy number]], and the sum of seven consecutive primes (97 + 101 + 103 + 107 + 109 + 113 + 127).

==== 758 ====
758 = 2 × 379. 

It is a nontotient and a prime number of measurement.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A002049|Prime numbers of measurement|access-date=2022-05-23}}</ref>

==== 759 ====
759 = 3 × 11 × 23. 

It is a sphenic number, a q-Fibonacci number for q=3,<ref>{{cite OEIS|A015474|2=q-Fibonacci numbers for q=3|access-date=2022-05-23}}</ref> and the sum of five consecutive primes (139 + 149 + 151 + 157 + 163).

===760s===

==== 760 ====
760 = 2<sup>3</sup> × 5 × 19.

It is a [[centered triangular number]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A005448|title=Sloane's A005448 : Centered triangular numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> There are 760 fixed [[heptominoes]].

==== 761 ====
761 is a prime number, an [[emirp]], a Sophie Germain prime,<ref name=":5" /> a Chen prime, an Eisenstein prime with no imaginary part, and a [[centered square number]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A001844|title=Sloane's A001844 : Centered square numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>
==== 762 ====
762 = 2 × 3 × 127. It is a sphenic number, a nontotient, a Smith number,<ref name=":3" /> an [[oeis:A111592|admirable number]], and the sum of four consecutive primes (181 + 191 + 193 + 197).

There are 762 1's in all partitions of 25 into odd parts<ref>{{cite OEIS|A036469|Partial sums of A000009 (partitions into distinct parts)}}</ref> There are [[Six nines in pi|Six nines in the decimal representation of pi]] after the 762nd digit.

==== 763 ====
763 = 7 × 109. 

It is the sum of nine consecutive primes (67 + 71 + 73 + 79 + 83 + 89 + 97 + 101 + 103). There are 763 degree-8 permutations of order exactly 2.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A001189|Number of degree-n permutations of order exactly 2|access-date=2022-05-23}}</ref>

==== 764 ====
764 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 191. It is a [[Telephone number (mathematics)|telephone number]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A000085|title=Sloane's A000085 : Number of self-inverse permutations on n letters, also known as involutions|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>

==== 765 ====
765=3<sup>2</sup> × 5 × 17. 

It is an octagonal pyramidal number.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A002414|Octagonal pyramidal numbers|access-date=2022-05-23}}</ref>

It is a [[Japanese language|Japanese]] word-play for [[Namco]].

==== 766 ====
766 = 2 × 383. It is a [[centered pentagonal number]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A005891|title=Sloane's A005891 : Centered pentagonal numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> a nontotient, and the sum of twelve consecutive primes (41 + 43 + 47 + 53 + 59 + 61 + 67 + 71 + 73 + 79 + 83 + 89).

==== 767 ====
767 = 13 × 59. It is a [[palindromic number]] and a [[Thabit number]]  because 767 = 2<sup>8</sup> × 3  − 1

==== 768 ====
768 = 2<sup>8</sup> × 3.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A007283|2=a(n) = 3*2^n|access-date=2022-05-30}}</ref>  It is the sum of eight consecutive primes (79 + 83 + 89 + 97 + 101 + 103 + 107 + 109).

==== 769 ====
769 is a prime number, a Chen prime, a lucky prime,<ref name=":6" /> and a [[Proth prime]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A080076|title=Sloane's A080076 : Proth primes|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>

===770s===

==== 770 ====
770 = 2 × 5 × 7 × 11. It is a nontotient and a Harshad number.

<math>\sum_{n=0}^{10} 770^{n}</math> is prime<ref>{{cite OEIS|A162862|Numbers n such that n^10 + n^9 + n^8 + n^7 + n^6 + n^5 + n^4 + n^3 + n^2 + n + 1 is prime|access-date=2022-05-30}}</ref>

It [[770 Eastern Parkway#Symbolism of "770"|holds special importance]] in the [[Chabad]]-Lubavitch [[Hasidic Judaism|Hasidic movement]].

==== 771 ====
771 = 3 × 257.

It is sum of three consecutive primes in [[arithmetic progression]] (251 + 257 + 263). Since 771 is the product of the distinct [[Fermat prime]]s 3 and 257, a [[regular polygon]] with 771 sides can be constructed using [[compass and straightedge]], and <math>\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{771}\right)</math> can be written in terms of square roots.

==== 772 ====
772 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 193.

772!!!!!!+1 is prime.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A085150|Numbers n such that n!!!!!!+1 is prime|access-date=2022-05-30}}</ref>

==== 773 ====
773 is a prime number, an Eisenstein prime with no imaginary part, a [[oeis:A006450|prime index prime]], and a [[tetranacci number]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A000078|title=Sloane's A000078 : Tetranacci numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>
* the sum of the number of cells that make up the convex, regular 4-polytopes

==== 774 ====
774 = 2 × 3<sup>2</sup> × 43. It is a nontotient, a Harshad number, and the totient sum for first 50 integers

==== 775 ====
775 = 5<sup>2</sup> × 31. It is a member of the [[Mian–Chowla sequence]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A005282|title=Sloane's A005282 : Mian-Chowla sequence|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>

==== 776 ====
776 = 2<sup>3</sup> × 97.

It is a [[refactorable number]]. There are 776 compositions of 6 whose parts equal to q can be of q<sup>2</sup> kinds.<ref>{{OEIS|A033453|access-date=2022-05-30}}</ref>

==== 777 ====
{{Main|777 (number)}}

==== 778 ====
778 = 2 × 389. It is a nontotient and a Smith number.<ref name=":3" />

==== 779 ====
779 = 19 × 41. It is a [[highly cototient number]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A100827|title=Sloane's A100827 : Highly cototient numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>

===780s===

==== 780 ====
780 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 3 × 5 × 13. It is a [[hexagonal number]],<ref name=":2" /> a [[Harshad number]], and the 39th [[triangular number]].<ref name=":1" /> It is the sum of four consecutive [[prime number|primes]] in a [[Prime quadruplet|quadruplet]] (191, 193, 197, and 199) and the sum of ten consecutive primes (59 + 61 + 67 + 71 + 73 + 79 + 83 + 89 + 97 + 101).

780 and 990 are the fourth smallest pair of triangular numbers whose sum and difference (1770 and 210) are also triangular.

==== 781 ====
781 = 11 × 71. It is a zero of the [[Mertens function]] and a lazy caterer number {{OEIS|id=A000124}} It is the sum of powers of 5, or equivalently, repdigit in base 5 (11111)
==== 782 ====
782 = 2 × 17 × 23. It is a sphenic number, a nontotient, a [[pentagonal number]],<ref name=":4" /> and a Harshad number.
==== 783 ====
783 = 3<sup>3</sup> × 29. It is a [[heptagonal number]].

==== 784 ====
784 = 2<sup>4</sup> × 7<sup>2</sup>. It is a [[happy number]].

Since 784=28<sup>2</sup>, 784 is a perfect square. It is the sum of the cubes of the first seven positive integers;  <math>1^3+2^3+3^3+4^3+5^3+6^3+7^3=784</math>.

==== 785 ====
785 = 5 × 157. It is a zero of the Mertens function. There are 785 series-reduced planted trees with 6 leaves of 2 colors.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A050381|Number of series-reduced planted trees with n leaves of 2 colors|access-date=2022-05-24}}</ref>

==== 786 ====
{{Main|786 (number)}}

==== 787 ====
787 is a prime number, a Chen prime, a [[lucky prime]],<ref name=":6" /> a palindromic prime, and the sum of five consecutive primes (149 + 151 + 157 + 163 + 167).
==== 788 ====
788 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 197. 

It is a nontotient. There are 788 compositions of 12 into parts with distinct multiplicities.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A242882|Number of compositions of n into parts with distinct multiplicities|access-date=2022-05-24}}</ref>

==== 789 ====
789 = 3 × 263. It is a [[Blum integer]] and the sum of three consecutive primes (257 + 263 + 269).

===790s===

==== 790 ====
790 = 2 × 5 × 79. It is a sphenic number, a nontotient, an [[aspiring number]],<ref>{{cite OEIS|A063769|Aspiring numbers}}</ref> and the aliquot sum of 1574. It is a Harshad number in bases 2, 7, 14, and 16.
==== 791 ====
791 = 7 × 113. It is a [[centered tetrahedral number]], the sum of the first twenty-two primes, and the sum of seven consecutive primes (101 + 103 + 107 + 109 + 113 + 127 + 131).
==== 792 ====
792 = 2<sup>3</sup> × 3<sup>2</sup> × 11. It is a Harshad number.
* the [[oeis:A006002|sum of the nontriangular numbers between successive triangular numbers]] 
There are 792 [[integer partition]]s of 21.<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A000041|2=a(n) = number of partitions of n}}</ref>

792=<math>\tbinom {12}5</math>, a binomial coefficient.

==== 793 ====
793 = 13 × 61. It is a zero of the Mertens function, a [[star number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A003154|Centered 12-gonal numbers. Also star numbers}}</ref> and a [[happy number]].
==== 794 ====
794 = 2 × 397.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A001550|2=a(n) = 1^n + 2^n + 3^n}}</ref> It is a nontotient.

794= 1<sup>6</sup> + 2<sup>6</sup> + 3<sup>6</sup>.

==== 795 ====
795 = 3 × 5 × 53. It is a [[sphenic number]] and a zero of the Mertens function.

There are 795 permutations of length 7 with 2 consecutive ascending pairs.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A000274|Number of permutations of length n with 2 consecutive ascending pairs|access-date=2022-05-24}}</ref>

==== 796 ====
796 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 199. It is a zero of the Mertens function and the sum of six consecutive primes (113 + 127 + 131 + 137 + 139 + 149).
==== 797 ====
797 is a prime number, a Chen prime, an Eisenstein prime with no imaginary part, a palindromic prime, a [[two-sided prime]], and a [[oeis:A006450|prime index prime]].

==== 798 ====
798 = 2 × 3 × 7 × 19. It is a zero of the Mertens function and a nontotient.
* the product of primes indexed by the prime exponents of 10!<ref>{{cite OEIS|A325508|Product of primes indexed by the prime exponents of n!|access-date=2022-05-24}}</ref>

==== 799 ====
799 = 17 × 47. It is the smallest number with digit sum 25<ref>{{cite OEIS|A051885|Smallest number whose sum of digits is n|access-date=2022-05-24}}</ref>
